Team — forwarding request from MedFolio. Key ask: 50% off for a 3-month pilot (~$22.5k). They will commit to an enterprise conversation in Q1 if pilot goes well.

Quick context:
- Pilot expected to generate ~120M tokens over 3 months based on their usage profile (two product teams, spike patterns).
- Risk: if we give 50% off with no floor, unit economics go negative for expected burst patterns.

Proposed commercial compromise from my side: 40% off with a 3-month fixed fee + a token overage rate at 60% of list per extra token, and a hard cap we can suspend at. Also an exec sponsor clause (MedFolio VP of Eng signs).

Marissa — can you run numbers quickly and tell me if 40% with an overage cap is approvable under existing guardrails? If it still needs VP/CFO signoff, please escalate and attach the pricing workbook.

Thanks,
Jonas
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot pricing question — MedFolio (need exception)

Jonas — ran the numbers (attached pricing-model-20260928.xlsx). Short summary:

- Baseline economics (list pricing): $45k for 3 months -> estimated margin ~42% after infra and SRE overhead.
- At 50% off flat without any consumption floor or tighter guardrails, margin swings to negative (~-12%) under median burst assumptions.
- 40% off with a $30k minimum guarantee + a hard token cap (we enforce via routing/suspend) brings margin back to ~8-12% depending on actual burst patterns.

Reqs/notes:
- Anything >40% discount or anything that removes minimum guarantee requires VP & CFO signoff per policy (discounts >35% require exec approval).
- If we do 40%, we should include:
  - Token cap and overage rate (pre-agreed)
  - 30-day termination/rollback clause if usage consistently exceeds modeled projections
  - Legal-approved SOW with acceptance criteria (Jonas to confirm)

I recommend escalating for an executive exception memo so we have an auditable approval trail. I've attached a short executive-approval-memo.pdf template to be filled with rationale and risk mitigation.

Marissa Cole
Head of Finance (acting CFO)
Redwood Inference
